name: Impacket GetUserSPNs - List SPN Accounts
description: Lists all domain accounts with a Service Principal Name (SPN) — the Kerberoasting target list. No -request flag means no tickets are pulled yet; this is pure enumeration. Only needs any valid domain credential.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHY KERBEROASTING WORKS ===
Kerberos design: any authenticated domain user can request a TGS ticket for any
SPN-registered service account. The DC encrypts the TGS using the service account's
NT hash. That encrypted ticket can be taken offline and cracked — NO lockout,
NO alerting in default Windows auditing (Event 4769 is logged but rarely monitored).

This is by design, not a bug. The weakness is weak service account passwords.

=== WHAT AN SPN IS ===
SPN maps a service to a domain account:
  MSSQLSvc/DEV-PRE-SQL.inlanefreight.local:1433 → service runs as sqldev
  HTTP/ACADEMY-EA-CA01.inlanefreight.local       → runs as iis_svc

Any account with an SPN is Kerberoastable. Priority targets:
  - SQL service accounts — often set with weak passwords and never rotated
  - Accounts with admincount=1 (were in a privileged group at some point)
  - Old PasswordLastSet dates — nobody is rotating, likely weak

=== THIS COMMAND: LIST MODE ===
No -request flag = LDAP query only, no TGS tickets requested.
Output columns: ServicePrincipalName | Name | MemberOf | PasswordLastSet | LastLogon

Look for: old PasswordLastSet + Domain Admins MemberOf = jackpot.
If sqlsvc is a Domain Admin with password set 5 years ago — roast it first.

=== LINUX vs WINDOWS ===
GetUserSPNs.py  (Linux)   → network-based query; needs creds + DC IP; no agent on target
Rubeus.exe      (Windows) → runs from domain host; /stats, /outfile, /rc4opsec flags
PowerView       (Windows) → Get-DomainUser -SPN for recon only (no ticket pull)
Use GetUserSPNs.py from Linux pivot; Rubeus when already on Windows host. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 22 (Attacking Active Directory Authentication).

references.title: HTB Academy - Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
OffSec PEN-200 - Penetration Testing with Kali Linux

recommended.note: Pull the TGS hashes for all SPN accounts.

defense.why_it_works: impacket GetUserSPNs lists domain accounts that have a Service Principal Name registered - the Kerberoasting target list - via LDAP.
defense.prerequisites: Valid domain credentials and LDAP access to the DC.
defense.impact: The set of Kerberoastable service accounts to target.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1558.003] LDAP queries filtering on servicePrincipalName / userAccountControl (Event 4662; Defender for Identity recon); one host reading roastable-account attributes.
defense.artifacts: LDAP query on servicePrincipalName; the SPN account list.
defense.prevention: Use 100+ character passwords or gMSA for service accounts; disable RC4 (force AES); audit and remove unused SPNs; deploy honeypot SPN accounts to catch roasting; Defender for Identity flags mass TGS requests.
defense.evasion: A single scoped LDAP query blends with normal directory reads; this step generates no 4769 yet.
defense.misconfiguration: Service accounts are registered with a Service Principal Name (SPN) but use weak, human-chosen passwords — or even share a password with other accounts. Any authenticated domain user can request a TGS for any SPN account, receiving a blob encrypted with that account's NTLM hash. The SPN registration itself is not the flaw; the flaw is weak passwords on SPN accounts and permitting RC4 encryption (which produces a shorter, faster-to-crack blob).
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Service account set up manually with a weak password + SPN
# Attacker can find these with:
Get-ADUser -Filter {ServicePrincipalName -ne '$null'} -Properties ServicePrincipalName,PasswordLastSet

# Bad state — password set 4 years ago, RC4 permitted:
# Name: svc_sql  PasswordLastSet: 2020-01-15  SPN: MSSQLSvc/db01.corp.local:1433
# RC4 (0x17) requested in TGS ticket — short hash, GPU-crackable

# Confirming RC4 is available:
Get-ADUser svc_sql -Properties msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes
# msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes: 0 (= RC4+AES both permitted if 0 or blank)
defense.secure_config:
# Fix 1 — Use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA): 240-char random passwords,
# auto-rotated by AD, no human ever knows the password
New-ADServiceAccount -Name gmsa_sql -DNSHostName sql.corp.local \
    -PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword 'db-servers-grp'
Install-ADServiceAccount gmsa_sql

# Fix 2 — For legacy accounts that must keep SPNs:
# Set a 100+ character random password (AD max is 127 chars):
$pw = [System.Web.Security.Membership]::GeneratePassword(127,20)
Set-ADAccountPassword svc_sql -NewPassword (ConvertTo-SecureString $pw -AsPlainText -Force)

# Fix 3 — Disable RC4, require AES-only:
Set-ADUser svc_sql -KerberosEncryptionType AES128,AES256
# msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes = 24 (AES128+AES256 only)
